leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations contain a single prize part on B022 (GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies) naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Shared: a discovery-centred citation tied to the physiology and the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and the view that maturity is not in doubt given human physiology, randomized outcome trials and routine care. Not shared: citation wording differs (some stress type 2 diabetes and obesity, others diabetes and obesity generally, and Wahren-Herlenius, Perlmann and Linnarsson tie it explicitly to the active form), and members differ in how much they regard the exclusion of Knudsen as a real cost rather than a technicality. No member proposes a second prize part in round 1; several raise a two-part prize only as a question.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B022 as their preferred configuration with the same three names (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov), and each states that the case rests on the science and not on the unanimity of the opening ballots.
All six describe the GLP-1 discovery as mature and independently confirmed in human physiology and large outcome trials (glycaemia, body weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints).

All six name attribution as the weakest point of B022: Habener is outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority is described as contested, and Knudsen is excluded by the three-laureate limit. No member claims to have verified the priority record independently.

Perlmann proposes the two-name June and Sadelain version of B003, and El Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius each say in their responses that it is cleaner or more defensible than the three-name version with Rosenberg.
Members agree that Hall is the essential name for B006 and that Sabatini's inclusion is uncertain; no member ranks B006 above B022.
scientific_disputes: Whether the second-ranked alternative should be a therapeutic modality with proven patient benefit (B003 CAR-T, listed as an alternative by El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius) or a clean basic-science discovery (B050 unfolded protein response, listed by Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius). Sandberg weighs proven patient benefit and keeps CAR-T slightly ahead; Svenningsson and, in part, Linnarsson value the compact two-person attribution of B050; El Manira calls the medical consequence of B050 indirect.

Whether the UPR (B050) has a sufficiently direct disease link, given that its medical consequence is described as indirect or mostly conceptual by El Manira, Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius, while Svenningsson points to relevance for diabetes, neurodegeneration and secretory physiology.

Whether the original chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar and others, not on the credited list) is a gap serious enough to weaken B003 this year; Perlmann says it counts against the case, Linnarsson calls it serious enough to hold CAR-T as an alternative rather than a co-prize.

Whether optogenetics (B034, El Manira's third alternative) can be reduced to three names without omitting a decisive contributor; Linnarsson, Perlmann, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius all say it cannot, and several note the disease link is early.

Whether cGAS-STING (B021) has enough clinical validation; Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson describe therapeutic translation as unproven, while Wahren-Herlenius ranks it fourth as an original mechanism.

Whether mTOR signalling (B006) is held back mainly by narrower direct therapeutic impact (El Manira, Linnarsson) or by unsettled allocation among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini (Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius).
attribution_disputes: B022: Habener is not among the credited names, and Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested in the public record. Wahren-Herlenius and Linnarsson argue Mojsov belongs in the trio; Perlmann says her inclusion rests on a priority question that cannot be settled from the ballots.

B022: Knudsen's peptide engineering (liraglutide, semaglutide) is excluded by the three-laureate cap. Sandberg and El Manira see her contribution as a different kind of work, more naturally recognised separately; Linnarsson, Perlmann and Svenningsson argue the exclusion is a substantive cost that should not be treated as neutral, with Linnarsson noting Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance.

B003: Perlmann proposes June and Sadelain only; Sandberg's opening credited Rosenberg alongside them and El Manira included him to keep a three-person set. Both later accept the two-name logic, so the ballot differs in laureates between the opening trio and the narrower configuration.

B006: Svenningsson's opening pairing of Hall and Schreiber is disputed. Perlmann argues Schreiber's rapamycin-FKBP12 work was a route to the target and not the discovery of growth control; Sandberg sees Sabatini's mTORC1 work as the stronger complement; Linnarsson notes earlier rapamycin work (Heitman, Sehgal) is outside the credit.

B021: Wahren-Herlenius treats Sun, Wu and Ishikawa as trainees of lesser weight than Chen and Barber, while Perlmann and Sandberg dispute that reading and say the credited list reflects their central experimental roles.
B050: mammalian UPR branches (PERK, ATF6, Ron and Kaufman) lie outside the credited names Mori and Walter, according to El Manira.
maturity_disputes: B022 is described by all six as mature; no member raises a maturity objection.
B021 (cGAS-STING) is described as early on therapeutic grounds by Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson.

B006 (mTOR): Linnarsson says the broader therapeutic promise of mTOR modulation is still emerging beyond transplantation and some oncology; El Manira says the direct therapeutic consequence is narrower than the conceptual reach.
B050 (UPR): El Manira, Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius describe the clinical payoff as indirect or mostly conceptual even though the mechanism has been confirmed for about 25 years (Sandberg).
B034 (optogenetics): the methodological impact is undisputed, but Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius describe the link to disease as early.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses roughly twenty co-authored works with Perlmann (count not audited) and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard, who is not a shortlisted name; he does not see either as requiring recusal.
Perlmann discloses co-authorship with Ronald Evans (not shortlisted) and some publications with Svenningsson and El Manira; he does not consider these a recusal issue for any shortlisted ballot.
El Manira discloses a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, a 2009 paper with Perlmann and work with Patrik Ernfors, none related to a shortlisted candidate.

Linnarsson discloses a 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and eight recorded co-authored works with Sandberg (count not audited); Sandberg separately discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen. Neither involves a credited name on the shortlist.
Wahren-Herlenius discloses co-authorship with Vijay Kuchroo and Sven-Erik Sonesson, neither on any shortlisted ballot.

Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius refer to concerns about the conduct or circumstances of a TOR candidate (understood to mean Sabatini) raised by colleagues; the round-1 files do not document what these circumstances are, and Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius say they cannot assess them from the supplied evidence. This is a process flag and not a finding.
questions_for_round2: Is the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio defensible given Habener's absence from the credited names and the contested priority for the active GLP-1 peptide, and what specific evidence in the dossier would settle Mojsov's standing?

Should the B022 citation honour only the physiology and active peptide, or should the committee consider a two-part prize or an explicit acknowledgement that drug development (Knudsen) is not being recognised?

If a second prize part is considered, would it be B003 (June and Sadelain, or with Rosenberg) or B050 (Mori and Walter), and how would the three-person ceiling be applied if B022 were reduced to two names?

Does the absence of the original chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar and others) from the credited names disqualify B003 for this year, or can a June and Sadelain citation be worded to be fair to that earlier work?
How should the committee weigh indirect medical impact (B050, B006) against demonstrated therapeutic impact (B003, B009) once B022 is settled?

Can the concerns raised about a TOR candidate be assessed on documented evidence at all, and if not, can B006 be considered on a Hall-centred configuration alone, and with which second name, Schreiber or Sabatini?
Is a three-person optogenetics configuration (B034) achievable without omitting a decisive contributor, or should it be set aside for this year?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one clear convergence and one open field. All six members prefer the same B022 configuration with the same three names and identify the same attribution weaknesses (Habener, Mojsov's priority, Knudsen). Below that, the explicit alternatives cluster on B003 and B050, with single mentions of B034 (El Manira) and B006 (Svenningsson). The main open questions for round 2 are the strength of the GLP-1 attribution record, whether a second prize part is wanted, and which alternative, if any, is better defended on both merit and attribution.
